findings.ours: The timestamp and the delivery ticks are subviews of the bubble, laid out at its bottom-right inside the content box (TGChatViewController.m:1150 adds `time` to `self.bubble`; :5745-5760 frames it at `bubbleW - timeW - kPadH`; :1097 adds `ticks` to the bubble).
findings.theirs: The date label, its translucent badge plate and the whole status (tick/clock/unsent) container live on the cell's contentView, OUTSIDE the bubble: incoming at `bodyFrame.origin.x + bodyFrame.size.width + 12`, outgoing at `bodyFrame.origin.x - 26 - retinaPixel - dateWidth`, y `bodyFrame bottom - 22`, with a 21 pt badge behind it (`messageDateBadgeIncoming` / `messageDateBadgeOutgoing`).
findings.citation: TGConversationMessageItemView.mm:3069-3079 and :3107; badge image at :2186; views added to contentView at :437-469
findings.fix: Move `time`, the date badge and `ticks` out of `cell.bubble` onto `cell.contentView`. Incoming: dateX = bubbleRight + 12; outgoing: dateX = bubbleLeft - 26 - dateWidth. dateY = bubbleBottom - 22. Behind it draw a 21 pt-tall stretchable badge starting at dateX-10 with width dateWidth+16 (incoming) or at dateX-5 with width dateWidth+29 (outgoing, the extra 29 holds the ticks). Ticks sit in that badge at x = dateRight - 30.

findings.ours: The message list is a flat run of bubbles with nothing between days; there is no date row anywhere in the data source (TGChatViewController.m:4933-4972 heightForRow has cases only for media/service/poll/etc., no date item; no day-grouping code exists in the file).
findings.theirs: The conversation model interleaves TGConversationDateItem rows of height 27 between days, drawn as a centred `systemMessageBackground` plate with the day string in bold system 13, white, shadow offset (0,1), plate inset -10/+20 around the label.
findings.fix: Insert a synthetic day row into `self.messages` whenever the calendar day changes between adjacent messages. Row height 27; centred label bold system 13 white with shadowOffset (0,1); plate is the label rect inset by -10 horizontally, -2 vertically, height = plate art height, centred on the row (`(rowH - labelH)/2 - 1`).

findings.ours: No "Unread messages" divider is ever drawn; opening a chat with unread history shows an unbroken list (no unread-item type in TGChatViewController.m; the only `unread` references are :6376 loadUnreadMentions).
findings.theirs: TGConversationUnreadItem is a 34 pt row: full-width `ConversationNewMessagesDivider.png` at y 3, a centred bold system 13 label in 0x506e8d with a 0xffffff/0.6 shadow at (0,1), and `ConversationNewMessagesDividerArrow.png` right-aligned at `width - arrowW - 7`, y `13 + retinaPixel`.
findings.fix: Add a divider row at the first unread message. Height 34; label bold system 13, colour 0x506E8D, shadow white 0.6 at (0,1), centred; divider strip full width at y 3; arrow glyph at right inset 7, y 13.5 on retina.

findings.ours: The group author name uses an invented six-entry pastel palette of floating-point RGB (TGChatViewController.m:4978-4986 `TGSenderColour`), indexed by `llabs(userId) % 6`.
findings.theirs: Eight fixed hex colours, keyed by an MD5 of "<uid><currentUserId>": 0xee4928, 0x41a903, 0xe09602, 0x0f94ed, 0x8f3bf7, 0xfc4380, 0x00a1c4, 0xeb7002.
findings.fix: Replace the palette in `TGSenderColour` with those eight hex values in that order, and index them by a hash of the sender id (the original MD5s the "uid" + "currentUserId" string; `llabs(userId) % 8` is acceptable but the colours must be exact).

findings.ours: The group author name is a label on the cell's contentView placed ABOVE the bubble (`[self.contentView addSubview:self.sender]`, TGChatViewController.m:1079), at y 2 with the bubble pushed down to top = 18, font bold system 12 (:1075).
findings.theirs: The author name is the first layout item INSIDE the bubble body, at `bodyPaddings.left, size.height + 2`, height 16, font `messageAuthorNameUIFont` = bold system 13; the bubble simply grows by `nameSize.height + 1`.
findings.fix: Draw the sender name inside the bubble as the first line: x = bubble text origin (bodyPaddings.left), y = kPadV + 2, height 16, font `[UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:13]`; add 17 to bubble height instead of shifting the bubble down by 18.

findings.ours: Group sender avatar is 28x28 with corner radius 3.36 (`kAvatarSide = 28.0f`, TGChatViewController.m:53; radius at :1093), and the bubble is shifted right by `kAvatarSide + 4` = 32.
findings.theirs: The conversation author avatar is 38x38, placed at `bodyFrame.origin.x + 4`, bottom-aligned to `bodyFrame bottom - avatarHeight - 1`, and the body is shifted by `avatarWidth + 4` = 42. The layout's max text width is also reduced by 40 when avatars are shown.
findings.fix: Set `kAvatarSide = 38.0f`; frame it at x 4 (relative to bubble box origin), y = bubbleBottom - 38 - 1; shift the bubble by 42; and subtract 40 from the max content width for incoming messages in group chats.

findings.ours: Message body text defaults to system 15 (`TGTheme.m:41-44` returns 15.0f when nothing is stored; used at TGChatViewController.m:1070, :4736, :4902).
findings.theirs: `TGBaseFontSize = 16` and the message text font is Helvetica at that size; the user-adjustable range clamps to a minimum of 16.
findings.fix: Change the default in `-[TGTheme messageFontSize]` from 15.0f to 16.0f and clamp any stored value to MAX(16, MIN(60, value)) as TGAppDelegate.mm:902 does.

findings.ours: Bubbles are inset 8 pt from each screen edge (`CGFloat x = mine ? (width - bubbleW - 8) : 8;` TGChatViewController.m:5398), and rows are separated by `top = 3` inside the row.
findings.theirs: `messageBodyMargins` is UIEdgeInsetsMake(0, 2, 3, 2): the bubble body box sits 2 pt from the screen edge, 0 from the row top and 3 from the row bottom. The 6 pt tail overhang is inside that 2.
findings.fix: Replace the 8 pt side inset with 2 pt on both sides, set the in-row top offset to 0 and reserve 3 pt at the bottom of the row instead.

findings.ours: Bubble content padding is symmetric: `kPadH = 10` left and right, `kPadV = 7` top and bottom (TGChatViewController.m:52-54).
findings.theirs: Padding is asymmetric and vertically tighter: incoming UIEdgeInsetsMake(5, 16, 5, 10), outgoing UIEdgeInsetsMake(5, 10, 5, 16) — 16 on the tail side, 10 on the other, 5 top and bottom. Minimum body size is 40x31.
findings.citation: TGTelegraphConversationMessageAssetsSource.m:1232-1240 (`messageBodyPaddingsIncoming` / `Outgoing`, written as 15+1 and 9+1); minimal size at :1228-1230
findings.fix: Replace `kPadH` with a per-side pair: leading 16 / trailing 10 for incoming, leading 10 / trailing 16 for outgoing. Set `kPadV = 5`.

findings.ours: The empty conversation shows a bare two-line grey label, system 14, centred, reading "No messages here yet.\nWrite something to start." (TGChatViewController.m:2049-2067).
findings.theirs: A 122x116 `systemMessageBackground` plate centred in the view, with `ConversationIconPlain.png` centred at y 23, and the string "No messages here yet..." in bold system 13, white, wrapped to a 110 pt width, bottom-aligned 8 pt from the plate bottom. It fades in over 0.3 s.
findings.citation: TGConversationController.mm:6141-6224 (container size at :6142, icon at :6206-6208, label at :6210-6224); string at en.lproj/Localizable.strings:333 ("Conversation.EmptyPlaceholder" = "No messages here yet...")
findings.fix: Draw a 122x116 rounded plate (the service-message wash colour) centred in the visible area, with the plain conversation glyph at y 23 and the label "No messages here yet..." — exact wording, single string — in bold system 13, white, `sizeThatFits:CGSizeMake(110, 1000)`, bottom edge 8 pt from the plate bottom. Fade the container in with a 0.3 s alpha animation.

findings.ours: Nav-bar subtitle is system 12 in white at 0.75 alpha (or secondary text when flat) with no shadow (TGChatViewController.m:1435-1439).
findings.theirs: The conversation status label is bold system 12, colour 0xe0eefd, shadow colour 0x3d5c81 with the bar's title shadow offset.
findings.fix: Set the subtitle to `[UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:12]`, textColor 0xE0EEFD, shadowColor 0x3D5C81, shadowOffset matching the title's (0,-1) in the skeuomorphic style.

findings.ours: Every timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `@"HH:mm"` date format (TGChatViewController.m:4707, :5471, :5497), so a device set to 12-hour time still shows 21:09.
findings.theirs: `stringForShortTime` branches on the device's 12-hour setting and returns "9:09 PM" / "12:05 AM" there, "21:09" only in 24-hour locales; the AM/PM suffix is drawn in a separate 9 pt font with a fixed 15 pt slot.
findings.citation: TGDateUtils.mm `+stringForShortTime:`; AM/PM font `messageDateAMPMFont` = system 9 at TGTelegraphConversationMessageAssetsSource.m:903-909, slot widths at TGConversationMessageItemView.mm:450-451
findings.fix: Replace the hard-coded formats with a helper that checks the locale's 12-hour flag and returns "%d:%02d AM/PM" or "%02d:%02d", and render the AM/PM suffix at system 9 in a 15 pt slot.

findings.ours: Message body text is 0x222222 (`TG_TEXT_PRIMARY`, TGTheme.m:223, used via `primaryTextColour` at TGChatViewController.m:5449).
findings.fix: Use 0x141617 for the bubble body label rather than the generic 0x222222 primary text colour.

findings.ours: Bubble timestamps use `timeColour` = 0x95999A, a light grey (TGTheme.m:225, :338; applied at TGChatViewController.m:5745).
findings.theirs: `messageDateColor` is 0x232d37 — a dark slate — because the date sits on a light translucent badge outside the bubble, not on the bubble fill. `messageDateShadowColor` is nil.
findings.fix: Once the date moves onto its badge outside the bubble, set its colour to 0x232D37 and drop the shadow.

findings.ours: Service (action) messages use system 12 on a 21 pt plate with corner radius 10.5, row height 30 (TGChatViewController.m:5085-5108, height at :4946-4947).
findings.theirs: Action-message text uses Helvetica-Bold 13 (`messageActionTitleFont`), colour white, on the stretchable `systemMessageBackground` art; the equivalent centred plate rows are 27 pt tall.
findings.citation: TGTelegraphConversationMessageAssetsSource.m:48-60 (`messageActionTitleFont`) and :289-295 (`messageActionTextColor` = white); row height at TGConversationController.mm:3817
findings.fix: Set the service label to `[UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:13]` and the row height to 27; keep the plate stretchable rather than a fixed 10.5 radius.

findings.ours: Maximum bubble width is `kBubbleMaxW + 2 * kPadH` = 260 pt for every message, with no reduction for outgoing messages or for group avatars (TGChatViewController.m:51, :5391).
findings.theirs: Layout max width is 250 pt total including paddings, reduced by 40 when avatars are shown on an incoming message and by a further 12 for outgoing messages (so 238 outgoing, 210 incoming-with-avatar).
findings.fix: Cap the bubble box at 250; subtract 12 for outgoing, subtract 40 for incoming rows that carry an avatar, then subtract the per-side paddings to get the text column width.

findings.ours: The message table leaves `scrollsToTop` at its default YES, so tapping the status bar jumps to the oldest loaded message (no `scrollsToTop` assignment for `self.table` anywhere in TGChatViewController.m).
findings.theirs: The conversation table sets `scrollsToTop = false` and installs a 1 pt off-screen `_scrollToTopInterceptor` scroll view that owns the status-bar tap; `scrollViewShouldScrollToTop:` instead scrolls the table to the BOTTOM (`contentSize.height - 28`) and returns false.
findings.fix: Set `self.table.scrollsToTop = NO` and add a 1x1 interceptor scroll view with `scrollsToTop = YES` whose `scrollViewShouldScrollToTop:` scrolls the table to the newest message and returns NO.

findings.ours: The group sender avatar is a plain UIImageView with no gesture recogniser (TGChatViewController.m:1091-1096), so tapping a participant's avatar in a group does nothing.
findings.theirs: The avatar view carries a tap recogniser wired to `avatarTapped:`, which opens that user's profile.
findings.fix: Add a UITapGestureRecognizer to `cell.senderAvatar` (userInteractionEnabled = YES) that pushes TGProfileViewController for that message's senderId.
